messages.subject: Does diag_pre_multiply() exist?
parts:
I've tried something like:

parameters {
    ...
    vector<lower=0>[4] sigma_u;
    corr_matrix[4] Omega;
}
model {
    matrix[4,4] L;
    matrix[4,4] DL;
    L <- cholesky_decompose(Omega);
    DL <- diag_pre_multiply(sigma_u, L);
    ...
}


but I got:

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=33, column=40

    DL <- diag_pre_multiply(sigma_u, L);

no matches for function name="diag_pre_multiply"

    arg 1 type=matrix

expression is ill formed

Are there any mistakes in my code?
Thanks
Sergio

messages.author: d4fb714af6c90658
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Does diag_pre_multiply() exist?
parts:
I have:
a) copied the rstan_2.0.1 tree to a new rstan_2.0.2 tree;
b) added:

add("diag_pre_multiply",MATRIX_T,VECTOR_T,MATRIX_T);
add("diag_pre_multiply",MATRIX_T,ROW_VECTOR_T,MATRIX_T);
add("diag_post_multiply",MATRIX_T,MATRIX_T,VECTOR_T);
add("diag_post_multiply",MATRIX_T,MATRIX_T,ROW_VECTOR_T);

to function_signatures.h;
c) rebuilt the tarball;
d) installed rstan_2.0.2 in .libPaths()[2].

Then I've tried:

parameters {
...
vector<lower=0>[4] sigma_u;
corr_matrix[4] Omega;
}
model {
matrix[4,4] L;
matrix[4,4] DL;
L <- cholesky_decompose(Omega);
DL <- diag_pre_multiply(sigma_u, L);
...
}

and it works. But I also tried:

generated quantities {
cov_matrix[4] Sigma;
Sigma <- diag_post_multiply(
diag_pre_multiply(sigma_u, Omega),
sigma_u);
}

and got an error:

Error : Invalid value of Sigma: Error in function
model49452e533851_kliegl_namespace::write_array(d): SigmaSigma is not
symmetric. Sigma[0,1] is -0.4943120689507427, but Sigma[1,0] element is
-1.4458

I can't understand why...

May I make a wish?
I think that functions that provide shorthand forms for common
expressions, but are also much more efficient, are strongly needed.
Replacing a plain matrix operation, such as D * L or D * Omega * D, with
two for loops just because those plain operations are very inefficient,
as you often say, is (boring and) error-prone.
I hope that diag_pre_multiply() and diag_post_multiply() will soon be
available and that something like diag_symmetric_diag_multiply() will
follow.

Cheers
Sergio

> May I make a wish?

Of course --- we have an issue tracker if you want to record

We're working on them. For every new function like this we
need double, reverse-mode auto-diff and forward-mode auto-diff
implementations. Ideally, with the auto-diff specialized to
the function at hand. They're easier to write if they're
just shorthand, but the diag_symmetric_diag could be made
much more efficient by not duplicating effort on the symmetric
calculations.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Does diag_pre_multiply() exist?
parts:
It's fixed in 2.2. You can now have a a model like this:

data {
vector[3] y[10];
}
parameters {
vector[3] mu;
corr_matrix[3] Sigma_corr;
vector<lower=0>[3] sigma_scale;
}
model {
matrix[3,3] Sigma;
Sigma_corr ~ lkj_corr(5);
Sigma <- diag_post_multiply(diag_pre_multiply(sigma_scale,
Sigma),
sigma_scale);
for (n in 1:10)
y[n] ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);
}

To use an estimate of Sigma with prior correlation matrix
concentrated (a bit) around the identity matrix.

- Bob
